payload.title: Ask optional help chat for scoped answers with source citations
payload.description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a help reader, I want an optional configurable RAG sidebar grounded in permitted documentation, so that I can ask questions and inspect the supporting sources.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Ask optional help chat for scoped answers with source citations
  Scenario: Answer within the configured scope
    Given chat is enabled for the current application and publication or knowledge base
    And the reader is authorized for a particular set of documents
    When the reader asks a help question
    Then retrieval is limited to that configured scope and the reader's existing access permissions
    And the answer cites accessible source pages or passages used to support its claims
    And unrelated publications, private drafts and unauthorized documents do not appear in answers, citations or snippets
  Scenario: Evidence or access is unavailable
    Given permitted documentation does not support an answer or access cannot be verified
    When the reader asks a question
    Then the sidebar states the evidence or access limitation without inventing an answer or widening scope
    And ordinary Help browsing remains available
  Scenario: A source changes
    Given a source is revised, withdrawn or its access permission changes
    When a later answer is produced
    Then retrieval and citation behavior follow the documented freshness and permission rules
```

Chat is optional and configurable. Design corpus/index scope, retrieval binding, source revision citations, permission enforcement, failure behavior, model/provider selection, privacy/retention and cost controls later. Use existing authorization rather than inventing access rights. This record authorizes no provider use, indexing or runtime work.
